annotations.text: The chosen direction: the landing column's grammar carried into the match. Nothing pauses; opening the column only takes the controls, and the ship stays live below it, so the wash is thin enough to watch trouble coming. It opens with Esc on a keyboard and the corner MENU key on glass, both of which already mean menu today.

The button, as the client already draws it: the key box every pressable thing wears, three bars for the mark, the word MENU beside them on a desktop because that corner is read. Dim until pressed, friend blue while the column stands. PLAYERS keeps it company in the row.
The settings stop opens the way the ship stop opens at home. This is the only home settings has: the landing keeps saying only who, where and what.

On a phone the word drops and the mark stands alone in a square of the same box; a thumb that has met this screen does not need the word. The column's 320 fits a 390 glass with margin, and RESUME lands where a thumb already lives.

The roads not taken, kept for the record: the corner-docked panel that never dims the fight, the console center card with settings a page deeper, and the hold-and-flick radial that costs a new grammar.
